A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UMed-LVLM and MAU research despite the revised title. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAU evaluation results, component ablations, localization and training analyses, generalization experiments, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds UMed-LVLM results on medical VQA and MedMNIST benchmarks, a coefficient search, and a multi-turn dialogue example.

M1.justification: Both versions use MedVInt initialization, abnormal-aware instruction tuning, and PPO-based rewarding with relevance, localization, and visual-attention rewards. Explicitly listing all three rewards and consolidating their equations in v2 clarify the existing procedure; the objectives and selected training settings remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PMC-VQA-test, and MedMNIST Pneumonia, Breast, and Derma. This substantially broadens coverage beyond MAU to additional question-answering and classification tasks, including ultrasound and dermatoscopy. Figure 6 also adds a multi-turn dialogue scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-4V supplied with ground-truth bounding boxes. New Tables 3–5 introduce comparisons with MEVF-BAN, CPRD-BAN, M3AE, PMC-CLIP, BLIP-2, Open-Flamingo, ResNet50, DWT-CV, and SADAE. MedVInt (SFT) and MedVInt (SFT&PPO) match the previously starred variants.

E3.justification: New evaluations distinguish open/closed questions and choice/blanking answers, introduce MedMNIST AUC alongside accuracy, and test GPT-4V with supplied boxes. Appendix E introduces five coefficient-pair configurations. Existing MAU split sizes and Appendix C training settings remain unchanged. v2 removes the stated 200-sample GPT-4V scope without specifying its replacement.

E4.justification: v2 adds a GPT-4V localization control, a reward/value-loss coefficient sensitivity study in Appendix E/Table 11, and a multi-turn case in Figure 6. MedMNIST also tests transfer to ultrasound and dermatoscopy absent from continual training. The earlier component ablations, localization curves, training-scale analyses, and held-out evaluations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds benchmark results in Tables 3–5, sensitivity scores in Table 11, and dialogue outputs in Figure 6. Table 2 replaces GPT-4V's 0.34 average on 200 samples with per-dataset scores averaging 0.31 under unspecified sample coverage, and adds 0.72 with boxes; this does not establish a same-setting decline. Original UMed-LVLM scores, including its 0.75 MAU average, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 consolidates the IoU and attention equations and shortens standard hidden-state/softmax exposition. The underlying probability model, reward definitions, normalization, and PPO objective are mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract newly claims a '58% improvement over the baseline,' quantitatively refining the headline performance claim. Table 2 already contained the corresponding 0.75 versus 0.17 accuracies in v1, a 58-percentage-point gap. The main method, dataset, and generalization contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains why supplying known diagnoses and abnormality locations makes GPT-4V suitable for generating dataset explanations despite weak direct diagnosis. It adds interpretations concerning ultrasound/dermatoscopy transfer and interactive consultation potential. The explicit data-availability limitation is removed, leaving computational resources as the stated limitation.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents annotation-based separation of training and test cases, manual correction of 13 generated samples, and the PPO implementation reference and coefficient search. These disclosures do not establish revised MAU splits or a newly performed review. Appendix C's optimizer, learning rates, batches, epochs, sampling parameters, and hardware are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds clinician preference alignment, MMedPO, RULE, MedTrinity-25M, and CARES, distinguishing their approaches from abnormal-region-guided optimization. References for new benchmarks and comparison methods also appear. The established LVLM and reinforcement-learning positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title from 'Training' to 'Improving,' condenses instruction-tuning and reward explanations, replaces several numbered subsections with run-in headings, and moves initialization/forgetting motivation into the introduction. The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark Tables 3–5, coefficient-search Table 11, and dialogue Figure 6. It redraws Figures 1–2, corrects Figure 1's ALR/VRR caption mapping, expands and regroups Table 2, and reformats or relocates retained tables. The original MAU examples remain as Figure 7.

improvement.justification: Evaluation beyond MAU and the GPT-4V bounding-box control provide broader and more targeted support for the paper's claims. Dataset-review clarification and coefficient-search reporting improve transparency. The net gain is limited by sparse protocol details for the added benchmarks, loss of GPT-4V sample-scope reporting, and removal of the data-availability limitation.
